answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable bond before it may trade, so a flood of fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Reputation then grows only from verified completed work, checked by randomly sampled peers, not from self-claimed history. Like a comet crossing a gale, a newcomer must survive real wind before it shines; the bond plus peer-checked work is the lantern that lets honest agents be seen while cheap copies stay in the dark.
